Income

Costs must be paid or Voat will go under. Without typical monetization strategies, which all too commonly reduce the presence of freedom, some alternative form of revenue must be found, usually within the userbase. Freedom-loving userbases are usually in the position to contribute, and are often willing, but they must have a reliable, secure, and ideally anonymous means.

Management

Even with costs paid, if there is no management, Voat will stagnate. If issues go unaddressed, or if desired features and functionalities never come, people will lose interest or lose hope and leave.

Content

Obviously, without the users posting content to Voat, there is no Voat. For a freedom platform to exist is one thing; for it to be truly meaningful it must be active enough to be known by those whom are in need of a freedom platform. Voat is not desperately wanting in this department, but if people lose interest or stop posting on account of failures to meet the management or income criteria, the content will begin to suffer and Voat's death will accelerate.

Growth

Short-term this is not as important, for as long as there is income, management for the sake of stability and functionality, and content, Voat can survive. However, a lack of any growth or change over time may cause whatever management there be to lose faith, and will eventually cause the content to grow repetitive or stale; an echochamber will form, and without those holding contrary positions with whom to converse and debate, no sense of productivity will be had, and this coupled with the stale content will cause the userbase to lose interest long-term. This does not mean that a point will be reached when no one will use the website; there will always be those who are content to at least go over news and current events with the stagnant and unchanging community. But even these types will use the website less and less frequently when there is no change, to the point where they may check in only once daily, once weekly, or even more seldom.

Content and Growth are the only realms over which the userbase has very much control. Those who do not post content can choose to begin contributing, thus adding more, and people can be determined to post various content from whatever media they consume or create on some kind of regular or semi-regular basis. Members of the community can also take action online and off to bring more to the community, or to encourage the community to be receptive to newcomers within reason. It is not that the community should be so tolerant as to jeopardize what makes the community free to begin with, but only so tolerant as to enable those who respect freedom at least to share in the contributing of content and the adding to discussions.
